t: Which of the following statements are true about carbohydrates? (i) Monosaccharides can be hydrolysed. (ii) The two monosaccharide units obtained on hydrolysis of a disaccharide can either be same or different. (iii) Polysaccharides are not sweet in taste. (iv) All monosaccharides are not reducing sugars.
s:
Monosaccharides are smallest carbohydrates that cannot be hydrolysed. So, statement (i) is not true.
Disaccharides are made up of two units of monosaccharides, so their hydrolysis will also give two monosaccharide unit that can be same or different. e.g., Sucrose → Glucose + Fructose Maltose → Glucose + Glucose So, statement (ii) is true.
Polysaccharides are polymers of many monosaccharides and have no sweet taste. So, statements (iii) is true.
Monosaccharides are categorised as reducing and non-reducing sugars. So, statement (iv) is not true.

t: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of
s:
Night blindness (nyctalopia) is caused by the deficiency of vitamin A. Vitamin A is a vital precursor for the synthesis of rhodopsin, a visual purple pigment found in the rod cells of the retina, which is essential for vision in dim light. A lack of this vitamin leads to impaired dark adaptation and can further cause xerophthalmia (hardening of the cornea).

Other options are incorrect because:
- Vitamin B₁₂ deficiency leads to pernicious anaemia.
- Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums).
- Vitamin E deficiency leads to increased fragility of red blood cells and muscular weakness.

Correct Answer: (B) vitaminA
